record.paper_title: Zero-Temperature Dynamics of Ising Spin Systems Following a Deep Quench: Results and Open Problems
record.original_question: Consider a zero-temperature stochastic ±J Ising spin system with nearest-neighbor Hamiltonian H = −∑Jxy σxσy, initial spin configuration σ0 drawn from the symmetric Bernoulli product measure, and standard continuous-time single-spin-flip Glauber dynamics, where each coupling takes one of two opposite nonzero values J1 and J2 with J1 = −J2. On Zd, or on another lattice not already covered by the odd-number-of-neighbors type-F result, in dimension d ≥ 3, what is the dynamical outcome? In particular, is the ±J system type I, type F, or type M, and can the density ρF of finitely flipping sites in the ±J model be related to the corresponding density in the homogeneous ferromagnet on the same lattice?

evidence.quote: Consider the stochastic process σ t = σ t(ω ) corresponding to the zero-temperature limit of Glauber dynamics for an Ising model with Hamiltonian, H = − ∑ Jx,y σxσy .
The initial spin configuration σ 0 is chosen from a symmetric Bernoulli product measure (denoted Pσ 0), corresponding physically to a deep quench.

The densities ρF and ρI depend only on d, µ, and possibly lattice type, and of course satisfy ρF + ρI = 1. We characterize the triplet ( d, µ , lattice type) as being type F or I or M (for mixed) according to whether ρF = 1 or ρI = 1 or 0 < ρ F , ρ I < 1.
When J1 = − J2 ≠ 0, we call this a ± J model. (In much of the literature, ± J spin glasses refer to the specific case α = 1 / 2.)

3) ± J models on Zd (or other lattices except where each site has an odd number of neighbors) for d ≥ 3. There is little we can say about these right now, except that it would be interesting to relate ± J models to homogeneous ferromagnets on the same lattice. E.g., perhaps ρF (± J model)≥ ρF (homogeneous ferromagnet). If this were the case, then demonstrating that homogeneous ferromagnets are type F on Zd for d ≥ 5 would immediately resolve the question for ± J spin glasses on those lattices.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{L}$ be an infinite, vertex-transitive lattice (for instance $\mathbb{Z}^d$) of dimension $d \geq 3$. Place an Ising spin $\sigma_x \in \{-1,+1\}$ at each vertex $x$ of $\mathbb{L}$, and assign to each nearest-neighbor edge $\{x,y\}$ a coupling $J_{xy}$ which independently takes the value $J_1$ with probability $1/2$ and $J_2 = -J_1$ with probability $1/2$ (with $J_1 \neq 0$ fixed). The (formal) Hamiltonian is
$$H(\sigma) = -\sum_{\langle x,y\rangle} J_{xy}\,\sigma_x\sigma_y.$$
The initial spin configuration $\sigma^0$ is sampled from the symmetric Bernoulli product measure on $\{-1,+1\}^{\mathbb{L}}$, independently of the couplings. Run continuous-time zero-temperature single-spin-flip Glauber dynamics: each vertex $x$ carries an independent rate-$1$ Poisson clock; when the clock at $x$ rings, $\sigma_x$ is updated to the sign that lowers the local energy $-\sigma_x \sum_{y\sim x} J_{xy}\sigma_y$ (and is updated to a uniformly random $\pm 1$ in case of a tie).

For each vertex $x$ let
$$\rho_F = \mathbb{P}\bigl(x \text{ flips only finitely many times in } [0,\infty)\bigr), \qquad \rho_I = 1-\rho_F.$$
By translation invariance these probabilities do not depend on $x$. Call the system type F if $\rho_F = 1$, type I if $\rho_I = 1$, and type M if $0 < \rho_F < 1$.

Assume that $\mathbb{L}$ is not a lattice for which an "odd-coordination-number" argument already forces type F.

(a) Determine which of the three types (F, I, or M) the $\pm J$ system on $\mathbb{L}$ belongs to.

(b) Express, or otherwise relate, the density $\rho_F$ for the $\pm J$ model on $\mathbb{L}$ to the corresponding density $\rho_F^{\text{ferro}}$ for the homogeneous ferromagnetic model (all $J_{xy} = |J_1|$) on the same lattice with the same initial distribution and dynamics.
artifact.category_tag: Zero-temperature Glauber dynamics on spin glasses
artifact.status_search_result: The classification of the ±J zero-temperature Glauber dynamics on Z^d for d ≥ 3 (type F, I, or M) and the relation between ρ_F for the ±J model and ρ_F for the homogeneous ferromagnet appears to remain open. Known results cover d=2 (mixed type M) and certain odd-coordination lattices (type F via Gandolfi–Newman–Stein), but no general resolution for d ≥ 3 on Z^d has been found in the literature; recent works (e.g., 2025 hypercube study, 2009 Morris paper on Z^d with random initial conditions) do not settle the disordered ±J case in high dimensions.

status_evidence.title: Zero-Temperature Dynamics of Plus/Minus J Spin Glasses and Related Models (Gandolfi, Newman, Stein)
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes type M for d=2 ±J models and gives conditions on certain lattices in higher dimensions, but leaves the general Z^d, d≥3, case open.
status_evidence.claim: Original problem source treats d=2 and odd-coordination lattices; higher-d Z^d case not resolved.

status_evidence.title: Zero-temperature Glauber dynamics on Z^d (Morris)
status_evidence.snippet: Studies zero-temperature Glauber dynamics on Z^d for the homogeneous model with random initial conditions.
status_evidence.claim: Addresses homogeneous (not ±J) dynamics, indicating the disordered case is still under investigation.

status_evidence.title: Zero Temperature Dynamics of Ising Systems on Hypercubes (2025)
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work on zero-temperature Ising dynamics in high-dimensional geometries.
status_evidence.claim: Recent activity continues on related high-dimensional zero-T dynamics problems.
